claim: An already-entered old Ready save using an Enabled=true snapshot can replace the successful Disable Enabled=false record after Disable has reset public states/cancelled CTS, if its read/clone/update is interleaved in the selected order and both saves succeed.

anchors.SaveTargetFirmness: get Configuration IL_0006; snapshot local IL_000b; Clone IL_004b or IL_005a; only target setter IL_0052 or IL_0061; Update IL_006e; no cancellation parameter/check in this synchronous helper.
anchors.UpdateConfiguration: set Configuration IL_0002 before Save IL_0008; returns current global Configuration IL_000e.
anchors.Save: Wait IL_0006; reads Configuration IL_000c and Serialize IL_0011; savedJson changed only after SaveConfiguration succeeds; Release in finally.
anchors.Disable: clone current config IL_0049; Enabled=false IL_004f/0050; Update IL_0055 before CreateNull IL_007f; public dictionary set IL_0090; CTS Cancel IL_00c8.
anchors.NullEnabledPredicate: CreateNullState closure reads manager.Configuration each invocation IL_0006, null->false IL_000e..0010, get_Enabled IL_0011; not a frozen Enabled boolean.
anchors.NullStateTransition: GetNextState Invoke predicate IL_0084; false loops to delay; true calls CreateNotConnectedState IL_0097. No unconditional cancellation throw before this true branch.
anchors.HostNextIteration: RunAsync creates a new CTS linked only to stoppingToken at IL_00a2 before GetNextState IL_00c6; per-side previous CTS.Cancel does not itself cancel all future CTS.

preconditions: Old Ready call already read a nonnull record with Enabled=true and is paused before replacing it.
Disable completes its own save and public-state/CTS updates normally.
Old helper is allowed to resume and its save succeeds; no later writer immediately changes Enabled again.
For later departure from Null: host remains running, reaches Null with a usable iteration, and predicate sees the replacement Enabled=true.
effects_supported: RAM Configuration may again contain Enabled=true.
With successful Save, the main R12 file may again serialize Enabled=true.
NullState predicate reads current manager value, so it can return NotConnected on a later usable iteration without requiring an explicit new Enable call.
not_supported: No actual overlapping calls or scheduler probability observed.
No claim about a strict delay or guaranteed transition after every Disable: outstanding GetNextState, Close, exception and host reconciliation still matter.
NotConnected is only a state object: discovery, gate policy, firmware, successful initialization, sends and physical pump/valve behavior are separate.
Does not cancel/retract already sent commands and does not prove any actual command was sent.
No exhaustive CLR memory-model or all method/caller proof; no original DLL execution.

manual_semantics_checks: Disable failure before successful Save return stops before public Null and CTS.Cancel.
UpdateConfiguration changes RAM before all modeled failures.
savedJson changes only after successful SaveConfiguration; earlier failure leaves cache old.
Target save catches failure and caller can enter send method; this is not an observed serial write.
A later successful whole-record save can include earlier failed target because it remains in RAM.
Unchanged Save still serializes before comparison, but skips open/write/flush/replace; Disable can continue Null/Cancel.
model_review.scope_caution: The synthetic tmp dictionary snapshots describe before-stage injection only; must not claim general real-IO failure leaves these exact temp or disk contents.

observations: Null departure is explicitly conditional on a live usable host iteration and later state coordination.
Five failure points explicitly injected before operations, with filesystem/physical effects excluded.
20 selected cases not confused with previous 20 cross-side enumeration.
